Femur|.text: It is the longest and strongest bone of the body, and accounts for approximately one-quarter of a person’s total height.
Femur|.label: 8.4 Femur

Femur|.text: The rounded, proximal end is the head of the femur, which articulates with the acetabulum of the hip bone to form the hip joint.
Femur|.label: 8.4 Femur

Patella|.text: A sesamoid bone is a bone that is incorporated into the tendon of a muscle where that tendon crosses a joint.
Patella|.label: 8.4 Patella

Patella|.text: The sesamoid bone articulates with the underlying bones to prevent damage to the muscle tendon due to rubbing against the bones during movements of the joint.
Patella|.label: 8.4 Patella

Tibia|.text: The tibia is the main weight-bearing bone of the lower leg and the second longest bone of the body, after the femur.
Tibia|.label: 8.4 Tibia

Tibia|.text: The medial side of the tibia is located immediately under the skin, allowing it to be easily palpated down the entire length of the medial leg.
Tibia|.label: 8.4 Tibia

Fibula|.text: The fibula does not bear weight.
Fibula|.label: 8.4 Fibula

Fibula|.text: It serves primarily for muscle attachments and thus is largely surrounded by muscles.
Fibula|.label: 8.4 Fibula

Tarsal Bones|calcaneus.text: The most superior bone is the talus.
Tarsal Bones|calcaneus.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|calcaneus.text: This has a relatively square-shaped, upper surface that articulates with the tibia and fibula to form the ankle joint.
Tarsal Bones|calcaneus.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|calcaneus.text: The medial calcaneus has a prominent bony extension called the sustentaculum tali (“support for the talus”) that supports the medial side of the talus bone.
Tarsal Bones|calcaneus.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|cuboid.text: The most superior bone is the talus.
Tarsal Bones|cuboid.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|cuboid.text: This has a relatively square-shaped, upper surface that articulates with the tibia and fibula to form the ankle joint.
Tarsal Bones|cuboid.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|cuboid.text: The cuboid bone articulates with the anterior end of the calcaneus bone.
Tarsal Bones|cuboid.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|cuneiform.text: The most superior bone is the talus.
Tarsal Bones|cuneiform.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|cuneiform.text: This has a relatively square-shaped, upper surface that articulates with the tibia and fibula to form the ankle joint.
Tarsal Bones|cuneiform.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|cuneiform.text: The talus bone articulates anteriorly with the navicular bone, which in turn articulates anteriorly with the three cuneiform (“wedge-shaped”) bones.
Tarsal Bones|cuneiform.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|talus.text: The most superior bone is the talus.
Tarsal Bones|talus.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|talus.text: This has a relatively square-shaped, upper surface that articulates with the tibia and fibula to form the ankle joint.
Tarsal Bones|talus.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|talus.text: The talus bone articulates anteriorly with the navicular bone, which in turn articulates anteriorly with the three cuneiform (“wedge-shaped”) bones.
Tarsal Bones|talus.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|Navicular.text: The most superior bone is the talus.
Tarsal Bones|Navicular.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|Navicular.text: This has a relatively square-shaped, upper surface that articulates with the tibia and fibula to form the ankle joint.
Tarsal Bones|Navicular.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Tarsal Bones|Navicular.text: The navicular and lateral cuneiform bones also articulate with the medial side of the cuboid bone.
Tarsal Bones|Navicular.label: 8.4 Tarsal Bones

Metatarsal Bones|.text: These elongated bones are numbered 1–5, starting with the medial side of the foot.
Metatarsal Bones|.label: 8.4 Metatarsal Bones

Metatarsal Bones|.text: The first metatarsal bone is shorter and thicker than the others.
Metatarsal Bones|.label: 8.4 Metatarsal Bones

Phalanges|.text: The toes are numbered 1–5, starting with the big toe (hallux).
Phalanges|.label: 8.4 Phalanges

Phalanges|.text: The big toe has two phalanx bones, the proximal and distal phalanges.
Phalanges|.label: 8.4 Phalanges

Patella|sesamoid.label: 8.4 Patella

Patella|sesamoid.label: 8.4 Patella

overview.text: Like the upper limb, the lower limb is divided into three regions.
overview.label: 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

overview.text: The thigh is that portion of the lower limb located between the hip joint and knee joint.
overview.label: 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

overview.text: The leg is specifically the region between the knee joint and the ankle joint.
overview.label: 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb
